title: Customizing and Saving Plots 🎨
description: Add labels, titles, legends, change figure size, styles, and export your visualizations.

slides.title: Make Your Plots Publication‑Ready ✨
slides.content:
# Controlling Appearance

Pandas passes most keyword arguments directly to Matplotlib. You can:
- Set `figsize`
- Add `title`, `xlabel`, `ylabel`
- Rotate tick labels
- Change color maps
- Add gridlines
- Position legends
- Save to file

slides.title: Figure Size & Title 📏
slides.content:
## `figsize` and `title`

```python
df.plot(figsize=(10, 6), title='My Chart', xlabel='X Axis', ylabel='Y Axis')
```

`figsize` is a tuple (width, height) in inches.

For more control, you can use `plt.title()`, `plt.xlabel()`, `plt.ylabel()` after the plot.

slides.title: Custom Size & Labels
slides.content: Plot with big size and labels:
slides.codeSnippet:
import pandas as pd
# Use previous df
df.plot(figsize=(10,5), title='Sales Over Time', xlabel='Month', ylabel='Units')
# The plot will show.

slides.title: Ticks & Rotation 🔄
slides.content:
## Rotate X‑Axis Labels

Use `rot` parameter (e.g., `rot=45`) to rotate tick labels for readability.

```python
df.plot(rot=30)
```

You can also use `plt.xticks(rotation=45)`.

slides.title: Gridlines & Legend 📌
slides.content:
## `grid` and `legend`

- `grid=True` – show grid.
- `legend=True/False` – show/hide legend.
- `legend_loc` – position ('best', 'upper right', 'lower left', etc.).

```python
df.plot(grid=True, legend='reverse')
```

slides.title: Grid & Legend
slides.codeSnippet:
df.plot(grid=True, legend=True, title='With Grid')
# Note: to change legend location you might need plt.legend(loc='upper left')

slides.title: Color Maps & Colormaps 🎨
slides.content:
## `colormap` Parameter

Specify a Matplotlib colormap for series colors: `colormap='viridis'`, `'plasma'`, `'Set1'`, etc.

```python
df.plot(colormap='tab10')
```

This assigns a different color to each column from that palette.

slides.title: Saving Your Plot 💾
slides.content:
## `get_figure().savefig()`

After creating a plot with pandas, you can save the figure using the underlying Matplotlib figure:

```python
ax = df.plot(title='Sales')
fig = ax.get_figure()
fig.savefig('my_plot.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
```

Alternatively, use `plt.savefig('name.png')` if you import pyplot.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Seaborn for Advanced Styling

`import seaborn as sns; sns.set_theme()` changes the overall aesthetic. It's built on Matplotlib and works with pandas plots.

3. Save the figure (comment out if in playground, but write the code).
